title: WORK STYLING Ueno — an open space you can use without booking, one minute from JR Ueno Station
lead: WORK STYLING Ueno is on the 2nd floor of the TT Ueno Ekimae Building, a one-minute walk from JR Ueno Station. Run by Mitsui Fudosan, this shared office has single-person rooms, meeting rooms for up to 12 and an open space. Everything below is based on the official website.
concept: A complete workplace on the 2nd floor, a minute from the station
WORK STYLING Ueno is on the 2nd floor of a building one minute from JR Ueno Station and five from the Tokyo Metro station. Places to work are gathered just above the ticket gates.
The open space here can be used without booking, so you can drop in and sit down straight away — or book a meeting room or private room in advance.

Being so close to the station, it is easy to drop in on the way somewhere.
The open space can be used without booking.
Seats of different shapes suit both solo work and short meetings.

There are several meeting rooms, so you can choose by headcount.

Single-person rooms are there for when you need to focus.
With a desk, chair and power, you can close the door and work.

word.title: What is drop-in?
body: Using a space on the day without a membership contract, paying by the hour.
WORK STYLING has a pay-as-you-go plan in 10-minute units, and the open space at this site can be used without booking.

name: H¹T Ueno
card: 3rd floor of Ueno Marui, with seats where you take off your shoes
title: H¹T Ueno — a 3rd floor in Ueno Marui with shoes-off beanbag seats
lead: H¹T Ueno is on the 3rd floor of Ueno Marui, connected to exit 5a of Ueno Station on the Tokyo Metro Ginza and Hibiya lines, one minute's walk. It is a satellite shared office run by Nomura Real Estate, with “Koagari” seats where you take off your shoes. Everything below is based on the official website.
facts: Open space 5 / 6 boxes (1) / 2 boxes (6) / 2 Koagari (1) / 16 rooms (1)
hero_cap: The corridor lined with room doors
concept: Shoes-off seats inside a workplace
H¹T Ueno has two “Koagari” seats: a Yogibo beanbag sofa with a Traybo lap table, used with your shoes off.
You can rest a laptop or book on the Traybo. There are no monitors here — these are seats for changing posture while you work.
steps: There are 16 single rooms, with doors lining both sides of the corridor.
The floor is finished in checkerboard tiles.

Koagari — a beanbag sofa and lap table
Six for one and two for six
There are six single boxes and two boxes for six.
A row of enclosures finished in wood and black.

word.title: What is Koagari?
body: The name H¹T gives to shoes-off seats at some of its sites, combining a Yogibo beanbag sofa with a Traybo lap table. The word recalls the small raised tatami platform found in Japanese homes and restaurants.
You can put a laptop or book on the Traybo; there are no monitors. H¹T Ueno has two.

credits: H¹T Ueno (Nomura Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.)
